title: Source A: 'Our Planet Promise' web page text, Harrowgate Mills (invented clothing brand)
text:
OUR PLANET PROMISE

We've always believed that great clothes shouldn't cost the earth. That's why, since 2019, every Harrowgate Mills jacket has been made with up to 40% less water*, and why we're aiming for a 50% reduction in packaging emissions by 2030.

We know we're not perfect. Nobody is. But we're learning, and we're listening: to you, and to the planet.

Last year, 2.3 million garments found a second life through our Re-Wear scheme. That's 2.3 million reasons to keep going.

Progress is made one choice at a time. Yours matters.

Join the journey. #WearItWell

*Compared with the 2018 Harrowgate Mills standard jacket. Figures independently verified; see our Impact Report for details.

title: Source B: the student's own draft body paragraph
text: The web page uses lots of persuasive techniques to make the reader trust the brand. Firstly, the use of statistics such as 'up to 40% less water' and '2.3 million garments' makes it sound very scientific and grabs the reader's attention. Secondly, the brand uses anaphora with 'we' at the start of every sentence, which makes the reader feel included. The writer also admits that they have cut their emissions by 50%, which shows they are honest and so the reader will believe them. The short sentences like 'Nobody is.' create a sense of urgency. Finally, the hashtag at the end shows the advert is aimed at teenagers who use social media, which is effective because it persuades them to buy the clothes.
